newsitem.title: USA: HP cuts prices on NetServer computers.
newsitem.headline: HP cuts prices on NetServer computers.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co on Wednesday said it is cutting prices up to 16 percent on its line of HP NetServer computer systems and up to 26 percent on server accessories.

In a statement, the computer industry giant said prices for its top of the line LX and LXe series NetServers were cut up to 14 percent. The LX line of computers are now expected to begin at retail prices less than US$8,640.
The LH Pro and LD Pro systems are expected to start at retail prices around US$2,925, and the NetServer E40 systems should begin at less than US$2,160.

"By lowering our prices across the board, we are reducing total cost of ownership for our customers and ensuring that they can obtain the highest-quality, most cost-effective solutions from HP," said Duncan Campbell, worldwide marketing manager for the company's network server division.

Hewlett-Packard said it cut computer memory list prices by up to 33 percent, while storage list prices fell by 11 percent on several products, including the company's nine gigabyte hot-swappable disk drives.
Also, several of its computer board and upgrade kits had their prices cut, too.
